To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the newly identified VanX inhibitors 6a and b are slow-binding inhibitors with high affinities, and that their binding to VanX involves conformational isomeric transition from a weak to a tight complex.

the newly identified VanX inhibitors, d-Ala-P-O-Phe (6) and d-Alu-P-O-Ala (6) dipeptide phophonates, are slow-binding inhibitors, and that the Vanx-inhibitor complex concomitantly underwent a conformational transition from an initial weak-binding adduct with fast dissociation to slowly convert to the final tight-binding complex with slow dissociation.

we have discovered three new VanX substrates with higher k(cat)/ K(M) values than that of its natural substrate d-Ala-d- Ala, and designed and synthesized two transition state analogs, 6a and b, as slow-binding VanX inhibitors, and used surface plasmon to directly measure the binding interactions of the inhibitors with the enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new slow-binding inhibitors of d,d-dipeptide dipeptidase VanX and the application of SPR for measuring slow binding kinetics of VanX inhibitors.
the design and synthesis of new inhibitors for the VanX enzyme, and the use of surface plasmon spectroscopy to directly measure their slow-binding kinetics.

the discovery of new VanX substrates, the development of new VanX inhibitors with higher affinity than that of the native substrate, and the elucidation of the molecular basis underlying the slow-binding interaction between VanX and its inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the slow-binding inhibition of VanX by dipeptide phosphates is a combined result of the conformational isomeric process of both the enzyme and the inhibitor and that the slow-binding process may be a general feature of the enzyme-inhibitor interaction.

both d-Ala(P(O))d-Phe and d-Ala (P(O))d-Ala are slow-binding transition state analog inhibitors of VanX, and the slow-binding process may involve a conformational rearrangement of both inhibitor and enzyme.
the VanX inhibitor 6a has a higher binding affinity to VanX than 6b because of the additional aromatic interaction of its phenyl group with the active site Phe residue of the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the slow binding of low molecular mass inhibitors to VanX can be directly measured by surface plasmons and the binding interaction is a result of conformational isomeric equilibrium between the initial but fast weak binding of inhibitors to VanX and the slowly formed tight-binding complex.
a slow-binding inhibitor of a target protein may be designed and synthesized by combining rational design and combinatorial chemistry.
the slow-binding inhibitors 6a and b are promising lead compounds for the design and discovery of new drugs against vancomycin resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

surface plasmon resonances can be used for the direct measurement of slow binding of low molecular weight inhibitors to a target protein, and this method can be applied in the study of slow binding inhibitors for other drug targets.
the slow-binding inhibitors can be identified by surface plasmonic resonance and that their binding interactions can be directly measured by this technique.

the slow-binding inhibitors of low-molecular weight are not only useful as a probe for studying the mechanism of enzyme-inhibitor interaction, but can be also developed as a potential lead for designing new drug candidates.
